title: I made a Townscaper-style town builder for iPhone where tapping the water grows a whole country map
author: LankyPepper665
selftext:
>Mina is a Townscaper-style town builder for iPhone/iPad (SwiftUI + SceneKit, no libraries). Almost all of it was written with Claude Code over \[N weeks/months\]. I'm not a \[Swift/3D\] specialist, so I wanted to share how this actually went, including the parts that went badly. Video is the current state.  
>  
>**What worked better than I expected**  
>  
>*A memory file the AI reads first.* A [`CLAUDE.md`](http://CLAUDE.md) with the architecture, the rules that protect saved towns (never reorder palette indices, only add optional fields to the save format) and a dated log of every task: what was asked, what was built, what was not checked. Without it every session re-broke something from the last one.  
>  
>*Letting it drive Blender by script.* The building parts (windows, doors, balconies, domes, even the landmarks) are authored by Python scripts that run Blender headless and bake ambient occlusion into a JSON the game loads. I describe a thing in words, it writes the script, renders a preview, I say "less boxy".  
>  
>*Audits.* Several times I said "find the invalid logic" and it ran three read-only review passes in parallel, then fixed the real ones. That caught things like a button that said "No room" on a brand-new install.  
>  
>*Debug hooks instead of hope.* The AI can't see my screen, so it added env-var hooks (open this sheet, render this style, grow this island) and takes simulator screenshots itself. One hook let it find a title-screen bug that cost half the frame rate (blocks still playing a pop-in animation never got merged into one mesh).
